newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S. Brunswick to trade local Russian shares.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Brunswick to trade local Russian shares.

text.p: U.S. firm Brunswick Securities Inc has won approval to trade ordinary shares in Russian firms with U.S. institutional investors, the company said in a statement.
BSI President Alexandra Vacroux said the decision by the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) marked a widening of the range of services of the firm.

BSI, the U.S. affiliate of Brunswick Brokerage, has traded American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) on Russian shares since May 1996, when it first received approval to deal in Russian securities cleared through a major U.S. broker-dealer.
ADRs are share look-alikes which allow stock in companies to be traded on foreign markets and which ease custody and settlement problems common in developing and emerging markets.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission must conduct a thorough review of a company's accounts before granting permission for an ADR issue and only a handful of Russian ADRs trade in foreign markets.
BSI and Brunswick Brokerage are part of the Geneva-based Brunswick Group, an independent investment house which serves institutional investors in the Russian equities market.
Vacroux said several major broker-dealer companies in the U.S. already trade in underlying Russian shares directly.

But BSI will be the first U.S. broker-dealer affiliated with an independent Russian-licensed brokerage to be granted authority to sell, self-clear and settle transactions in Russian equities to and for U.S. institutional investors, she said.
